text: Whoa, that thought's just gone. What did I even come in here for?
This happens so often, it actually has a name: the doorway effect.
Every time your brain crosses through a doorway, it files away whatever you were just thinking about.
So the second you step through, that thought gets left behind, and your head fills up with the new room instead.
String together a few doorways in a row, and it gets even easier to lose track.
Studies even found it happens when you walk through a virtual doorway in a video game.
Weirdly, if you walk back into the room where you started, that thought often comes right back.
